panels.visual: Serious, sober tone: a line of war captives, men, women and children in plain rags, arriving in the Athenian Agora under a heavy sky, led by a trader with a stick held low; faces tired and dignified, no cruelty shown, Glauka watching from a column
panels.caption: In classical Athens perhaps a third of the people were enslaved. Many were captives of war, or bought from slave traders.

panels.visual: A split scene of everyday labour: a girl fetching water in a jar from a fountain house, an enslaved man at a potter's wheel in a workshop, and a man keeping accounts on a wax tablet, quiet muted mood
panels.caption: Some worked in houses, shops and workshops, fetched water or kept accounts.

panels.visual: The Laurion silver mines: a dark cramped tunnel with low stone ceilings lit by tiny oil lamps, exhausted miners crouched with picks, deep shadows, heavy oppressive mood, no violence shown
panels.caption: The worst fate was the silver mines at Laurion, where thousands worked in cramped tunnels underground, often until they died.

panels.visual: Split panel: top, shining silver owl coins and a fleet of Athenian warships (triremes) at Salamis in 480 BC; bottom, citizens raising their hands to vote on the Pnyx hill while a small group of enslaved people stand outside the crowd at the edge, looking on
panels.caption: Laurion's silver paid for the warships at Salamis and the owl coins. Athens' glory rested partly on people who had no vote and no freedom.
